How long a call may take, in ms (30 s).
The most a response may be, in bytes (100 KB), so a huge one can't flood an agent's prompt; a larger one fails. File fields count apart.

tools.summary: Name this chat for what you found, once you have: people pick a run from a list by its name ("Nov 2 · Competitor cut 8%, we hold"). One short line, with the conclusion.

tools.name: schedule_routine
tools.summary: Make a routine: a message sent to an agent on a schedule, here, as the person you work for ("every weekday at 9:00, ask @researcher for the news on X", "remind me every Monday to send the report"). text is what's sent each time, written as the person would ask it; agent defaults to you. Give the person's timezone when you know it (ask when the time matters and you don't); without one, it's UTC. Where it posts: by default back in this chat (reminders, monitoring, anything that reads as one thread). Use post "new" when each run is its own piece of work to open later (a daily analysis), and give chat_name. Tell them what you set up, and where it posts.

agent.description: Who it asks; you, by default.

schedule.description: kind daily, weekdays or weekly (days, 0 = Sunday) take time (24h, "09:00"); hours takes every (how many); once takes at ("2026-11-03T09:00", in timezone); cron takes cron (five fields). All but hours take timezone (IANA).

post.description: same (default): always this chat; new: a new chat each run.

chat_name.description: With post new, what each chat is called: "Pricing response · {date}". {date}, {time} (its timezone), {run} and {name} are filled in each run.
